propositions: Infrastructure plans commit risky runtime mechanisms (service boot, credential authorization, dependency connection, readiness checks) into slow codified delivery loops (CI/CD, IaC apply, provisioning) without first proving them via fast out-of-loop experiments, delaying discovery of basic failures until the end of lengthy cycles.
No existing plan-review criterion rewards or enforces front-loading de-risk proofs (local runs, manual probes against real targets) before mechanisms enter the slow delivery loop.

T15 must establish a stack-agnostic, self-gating overlay that requires plans to name specific runtime-only risks and commit to proving each via the fastest available feedback path before codifying them.

T15 rubric applicability gates on codified slow-loop delivery, costly pass-through time, and runtime-only correctness; checks enforce risk naming, fast out-of-loop proof, prove-then-codify ordering, and scoped throwaway cleanup.
T10 production-hardening criterion must be partitioned to exclude transient de-risk experiments, preventing runtime cross-criterion overlap and keeping T10 scoped to durable infrastructure only.
Delivery must include registry generation, criterion documentation, writing-a-passing-plan guidance, and a recorded coach-move decision on the proposed out-of-loop-proof move.
